description: Locator strategy (founding doc section 5) and waiting strategy (section 6). The stability ranking and the wait playbook are single ordered-payload procedures. Hubs: hub_sf_locators, hub_sf_waits.

atoms.payload: [V-M] Locator stability ranking for Salesforce UI, most to least stable: 1) data-testid / data-* on components YOU own (getByTestId; attribute configurable via testIdAttribute) — unavailable on standard Salesforce UI. 2) Role + accessible name: getByRole('button', {name: 'Save'}) — the durable interface. 3) Field/object API names in attributes: [field-name='Industry'], [data-target-selection-name='sfdc.RecordField.Account.Name'], datatable [data-label='...']. 4) Custom-element tag anchors: page.locator('lightning-combobox'), records-record-layout-item, filtered by hasText. 5) Label text: getByLabel('Amount') — stable per org, breaks under i18n/renames. 6) SLDS classes ONLY as coarse state markers (.slds-spinner, .slds-modal_open, .slds-notify_toast), never as element identifiers (Summer '25 removed deprecated classes; SLDS 2 re-themes). 7) NEVER: generated ids, LWC scope attributes, positional nth-child, deep combinators into base-component internals, any XPath.

[V-M] data-testid attributes are NOT available on standard Salesforce UI — it is a closed ecosystem where you cannot annotate Salesforce-owned components. getByTestId applies only to your own custom LWCs. For everything Salesforce ships, plan around role + accessible name and API-name attributes instead.

[S exact attrs / V-M principle] Field and object API names surface in DOM attributes and are release- and i18n-stable: [field-name='Industry'] and [data-target-selection-name='sfdc.RecordField.Account.Name'] on record fields, [data-label='ColumnLabel'] on datatable cells. API names survive label renames and translations — prefer them over label text wherever they are present.

[V-O mechanism / S pattern] Scope locators to containers to satisfy Playwright strict mode — Salesforce repeats labels and buttons across regions (highlights panel vs details tab vs related lists vs modals). Patterns: page.getByRole('tabpanel', {name: 'Details'}).getByLabel('Phone'); scope ALL modal interaction to page.getByRole('dialog'). A strict-mode violation on Salesforce usually means missing container scoping, not a wrong locator.

[V-O] Playwright locators are lazy and re-resolved at every action — immune to the Lightning re-renders that invalidate stored element handles (Selenium's stale-element failure mode). Never store resolved element handles; always act through the locator. This re-resolution is Playwright's structural advantage on re-render-happy Lightning.

[V-M] Define every locator in exactly one place (a page object or component object) so each seasonal release's churn is a localized diff instead of a suite-wide hunt. Pair with the maintenance budget: 3 Salesforce releases per year will each move something.

[V-O/V-M] waitForLoadState('networkidle') is discouraged by Playwright and structurally wrong on LEX: boxcar gaps produce false-ready (idle while work is queued) and continuous beacons/hidden-tab traffic produce never-ready (timeout). Some practitioner guides still use it as a pragmatic first settle; the strict position replaces it entirely with app-visible-state assertions.

[V-M] The primary wait tool is auto-retrying web-first assertions on app-visible state. Target content: await expect(page.getByRole('heading', {name: recordName})).toBeVisible(). Spinners gone: await expect(region.locator('.slds-spinner')).toHaveCount(0, {timeout: 30000}). Toast: await expect(page.locator('.slds-notify_toast')).toContainText(/was (created|saved)/i). Modal closed: await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeHidden({timeout: 15000}). Rule: every wait names the app-visible condition it awaits.

[V-M] Surgical network wait for Aura actions: set up const responsePromise = page.waitForResponse(r => r.url().includes('/aura') && r.request().method() === 'POST') BEFORE triggering the action, then await it after. On portals match /sfsites\/aura/. Wait on URL + status only — never assert boxcar payload internals (the envelope is opaque and multiplexes unrelated actions).
[V-O] Platform toasts auto-dismiss after 4.8 seconds (9.6 seconds when they contain a link). Assert toasts immediately after the triggering action, or the assertion races the dismissal and flakes.

[INF] LEX navigations are pushState SPA transitions, not document loads. page.waitForURL() works for asserting arrival, but load-state events do not correspond to content readiness — wait for content (heading, region, record data), never for load events.

[S] Console apps: inactive workspace tabs have NO DOM at all until activated (Summer '25 lazy-load). After activating a console tab, wait for a unique element inside the newly activated tab before interacting — asserting on stale content from the previous tab is a classic console flake.

[V-M] Hydration risk (especially on LWR sites, which serve static snapshots that hydrate): an element can exist in the DOM before its event listeners attach, so an early click is a silent no-op — no error, nothing happens. Wait for a real readiness indicator (interactive response, aria state change, content update), never mere element presence, before the first interaction.
